Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Asset Management Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Asset Management's second quarter results. Joining me on today's call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; David Kim, Head of Distribution; and Emily Vargas, Head of Operations.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust net client inflows and market appreciation across our diversified platform. Our assets under management grew to $2.85 trillion, reflecting strong year-over-year expansion and underscoring the resilience of our strategies in a dynamic market.

Michael Chen: Thank you, John. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Asset Management delivered strong results in the second quarter. Our revenue was $3.4 billion, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher management fee revenue amid AUM expansion. Management fees came in at $3.2 billion overall for the year to date, but specifically for the quarter, they reached $1.42 billion, up 8% year-over-year and 3% sequentially. This reflects solid organic AUM growth of around 6% excluding market and FX effects, with total AUM hitting $2.85 trillion at quarter-end, up 12% from last year on $28 billion in net new money and favorable tailwinds in U.S. large-cap equities and alternatives.

Our average management fee rate stood at 42.5 basis points for the quarter, down 30 basis points year-over-year from 45.5 basis points, and flat sequentially. This moderation aligns with broader industry dynamics where passive products continue to draw flows at sub-10 basis point levels, but we're countering it strategically through product mix shifts. By asset class, equities drove $785 million in fees, up 10% year-over-year at 48 basis points average, thanks to inflows into active strategies like our Apex Global Equity Fund, which gathered $12 billion in net new money amid interest in AI-driven alpha. Fixed income contributed $412 million, up 5% at 35 basis points, with demand for our ESG-enhanced bond strategies in this rate environment. Alternatives, our margin powerhouse, added $185 million, up 15% at 85 basis points, powered by private credit and infrastructure platforms drawing $8 billion from institutions.

Geographically, the Americas generated 62% of fees at $880 million, up 9%, fueled by SMAs in wirehouse channels commanding 55 basis points. EMEA was 25% or $355 million, up 7%, with Luxembourg feeders capturing €15 billion from pension consolidations. APAC grew to 13% or $185 million, up 12% at 44 basis points, with strength in Japan ETFs despite China regulatory hurdles. To mitigate compression, our Fee Optimization Program using advanced analytics has uplifted institutional mandates by 2 basis points via ESG and risk premia services. We've also launched five new active ETFs, like the Apex Climate Transition at 25 basis points, and scaled SMAs and UMAs for 20-30% fee premiums, with $45 billion in new UMA mandates this quarter. We expect Q3 fees of $1.45 to $1.48 billion, holding mid-42 basis points with alt inflows providing upside.

Our expenses were $1.28 billion, up modestly 4.2% year-over-year from $1.23 billion. On average AUM of $2.85 trillion, this equates to 52 basis points, down from 55 last year. Compensation and benefits were $712 million, or 55.6% of total, up 3.8% on headcount growth to 4,250 in quant and sustainable teams, with merit increases and incentives tied to 12.7% organic AUM gains. Variable comp moderated via performance hurdles, and we're upskilling with our AlphaForge AI platform to boost PM productivity 15-20%. Technology and data services hit $248 million, up 12.5%, at 15 basis points of AUM, including $85 million for AWS/Azure cloud migration and $45 million for AI risk analytics handling rate shocks or geopolitical scenarios. Vendor consolidation saved $12 million, though ESG data licenses rose 18%. Distribution and marketing were $128 million, up 2.9%, efficient via sub-advisory with Schwab and Fidelity, and digital campaigns yielding 4.2x ROI on new ETF launches. G&A held at $96 million, flat, with outsourcing offsetting SEC and EU compliance upticks, and hybrid work cutting occupancy 8%. Amortization and other added another $96 million, up 6.1%, from acquisitions like Horizon Quant.

This discipline drove net income of $1.1 billion. Our expense ratio improved to a weighted average of 42 basis points as of quarter-end, down 8 basis points year-over-year and our 11th straight sequential gain. Calculated as total operating expenses over average daily AUM, excluding acquired fees per SEC rules, this beats industry benchmarks—Lipper shows 68 basis points for large-cap active equity, 18 for passive ETFs. We outperform Vanguard's 45 blended and edge BlackRock's iShares at 39 net. By silo: ETFs and index at 8 basis points on $1.17 trillion, with Apex Core S&P 500 ETF at 5 basis points on $450 billion, half of SPY, fueled by $120 billion YTD inflows. Active mutuals and SMAs at 62 basis points on $912 billion, down from 70, with 250 basis points alpha in large-cap growth. Alternatives at 95 basis points on $770 billion, competitive with Ares at 110. Regionally, North America at 38 basis points via 401(k) rebates and CIT migrations; Europe 48 with UCITS at 12; Asia-Pacific 55, led by ESG Japan at 45.

Drivers include 22% YoY AUM scale diluting fixed costs 15%, plus our $250 million tech roadmap: ApexFlow automating 85% middle-office for 28% trade cost cuts, AI surveillance saving $45 million, and State Street outsourcing yielding 10 basis points on $800 billion. Passive now 48% of AUM, blended in TDFs at 22 basis points capturing $50 billion flows. We guide full-year to 40-41 basis points on $3.1 trillion AUM.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Michael. Our AUM ended the quarter at a record $2.85 trillion, up 14.2% year-over-year and 4.8% quarter-over-quarter, our 11th straight positive organic quarter. Net inflows were $28.5 billion, up 22% sequentially, plus $32.1 billion market gains from risk asset rallies, modest $1.2 billion FX from euro strength, offset by $4.3 billion outflows in short-duration fixed income. YoY from $2.49 trillion on $112 billion cumulative inflows and $48 billion markets, beating industry 8-10%.

Breakdown: Equity $1.28 trillion, 45%, up 6.2% QoQ and 18.5% YoY on $15.2 billion flows; strong U.S. large-cap mirroring S&P 10.5%, EM ex-China like India Nifty 12%; Pinnacle Global Equity up 320 bps over 3 years; ESG ETF $4.1 billion. North America 55%, Europe 28%, APAC 17% from SWFs. Fixed income $855 billion, 30%, +2.1% QoQ, 8.7% YoY on $9.8 billion flows to intermediate/long duration like Core Bond $3.2 billion ahead of Fed cuts; outperforms Bloomberg Aggregate; ESG 40%; U.S. 60%, EMEA 25%, Asia LDI. Alternatives $570 billion, 20%, fastest at 7.9% QoQ, 22.4% YoY on $12.4 billion, private equity $8.5 billion from oversubscribed Fund VII $15 billion targeting 15-18% IRRs; hedge 8.2% vs HFRI 4.1%; real assets infrastructure; digital $2.5 billion ETPs. Multi-asset/cash $150 billion, 5%, +1.5% QoQ but -$9.9 billion outflows. ETF platform $420 billion up 35%; U.S. 60%, EMEA 25%, APAC 15%. Outlook: Q3 flows $30-35 billion, year-end $3.0-$3.1 trillion.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in alternatives and equities. We're navigating the current market environment by leaning into AI infrastructure, private credit, and ESG themes while managing rate volatility through active duration and credit selection. We launched the Apex AI Innovators ETF this quarter, and early reception has been positive, with $5 billion in initial flows blending quant alpha.

David Kim: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and alternatives funds, totaling $28.5 billion. Our efforts to expand our reach in Asia-Pacific and EMEA are paying off, as evidenced by $20 billion from APAC sovereign mandates and €15 billion EMEA pension flows via UCITS and feeders, plus U.S. RIA model portfolio adoption driving ETF growth.

Emily Vargas: Thank you, David. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure with the full rollout of ApexFlow on Snowflake and AWS, automating reconciliations and slashing processing costs 28%. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We're also focused on AI overlays for compliance and quant models, outsourcing to State Street, and hybrid models cutting G&A.

John Reynolds: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes our capital allocation framework across organic growth, inorganic tuck-ins, and shareholder returns. Organically, 45% of $1.8 billion YTD deployment went to high-ROIC tech like $300 million in Apex Alpha AI platform enhancing $250 billion equities for 120 bps margin gains, and APAC hubs for semiconductors/renewables ETFs yielding 15% IRR. Inorganic 30% or $540 million, like $400 million Horizon Private Debt adding $45 billion AUM accretive 50 bps to 52 bps blended fees, and seeds for infrastructure/digital alts. Shareholder returns 25% or $450 million via 8% dividend hike to $0.85/share and $1.5 billion buybacks at 15% NAV discount boosting EPS 4%. ROIC 18% over 5 years; outlook $1.5 trillion AUM by 2026, 60% FCF conversion.

For 2025, priorities are product innovation like three active ETFs and SMA pods; $250 million ApexNext AI for 150 bps alpha, tokenization, robo-upgrades; APAC JV with DBS for Sukuk, EMEA private credit; scaling alts $300 billion at 14% IRR and ESG to 20% AUM. Target 10-12% growth to $3.1 trillion, $120-140 billion inflows, 15-18% ROE.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Morningstar.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more details on AUM growth drivers and the asset class breakdown?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Alex. Happy to elaborate. As Michael noted, our $2.85 trillion AUM reflects 14.2% YoY and 4.8% QoQ growth from $28.5 billion inflows, $32.1 billion markets, minor FX, offset by fixed income rotations. Equity at 45% or $1.28 trillion led with 18.5% YoY on U.S. large-cap and EM strength, $15.2 billion flows. Fixed income 30% stable at 8.7% YoY, $9.8 billion to duration bets. Alts 20% fastest at 22.4% YoY, $12.4 billion including PE Fund VII oversubscribed. Multi-asset dipped on de-risking. ETF surge to $420 billion via RIAs; regional balance with APAC momentum positions us for $30 billion Q3 flows.

Alex Rivera: Thank you. And a follow-up on management fee trends?

Michael Chen: Absolutely. Fees up 8% to $1.42 billion at 42.5 bps, product-led: alts 85 bps growing share to 20%, equities 48 bps on active, ETFs 12 bps scaling. Regional uplift in APAC; levers like optimization and UMAs protect amid compression. Q3 guide steady.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Barclays.

Jordan Lee: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of your alternatives platform?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Jordan. Alternatives shone at $570 billion, 22.4% YoY growth outpacing peers per Preqin. $12.4 billion inflows: PE $8.5 billion from Fund VII 15-18% IRRs via AI infra secondaries; hedge 8.2% on dispersion; real assets energy transition; new digital ETPs $2.5 billion post-ETF approvals. Institutional-heavy, diversified regions, blending with evergreen feeders for retail access.

Jordan Lee: And how is the new AI Innovators ETF performing relative to expectations?

David Kim: Exceeding, Jordan. $5 billion AUM already in Q2 launch, 50 bps fee capturing AI hype with NVDA/TSM tilts and ML alpha. Distribution via wirehouses and RIAs mirroring iShares success, early flows beat targets by 25%, positioning for $10 billion year-end.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with Goldman Sachs.

Taylor Brooks: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Emily Vargas: Good morning, Taylor. Our efficiencies stem from $250 million tech roadmap: ApexFlow automated 85% middle-office, cutting trade costs 28% to 1.5 bps; AI surveillance saved $45 million, ML rebalancing preserved alpha; State Street for 10 bps savings. Scale diluted fixed costs 15%, hybrid/outsourcing flat G&A. Expense ratio to 42 bps proves it—Vanguard costs with BlackRock innovation, margins to 52%.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to John Reynolds for closing remarks.

John Reynolds: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
